from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):

                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Load Assets

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.place_at_grid(metronome, 'A3', scale_factor=0.3)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(c1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # But it lacks a precise pitch.
        peak1 = Dot(color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(peak1, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        # Using simple periodic marker for repetition peaks
        peaks = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FF5733").move_to(self.grid['C3'] + RIGHT * i * 0.2) for i in range(5)])
        self.play(Create(peak1), *[Create(p) for p in peaks])
        self.lecture[1].set_color(c2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A long note has precise pitch.
        wave2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(wave2, 'E3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(tuning_fork, 'E3', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Create(wave2), FadeIn(tuning_fork))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(c3)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Fourier Bridge", [
            "Fourier transform maps time to frequency.",
            "Signals decompose into constituent sine waves.",
            "Think of it like a prism."
        ])
        
        # Setup objects
        signal_waveform = FunctionGraph(lambda t: np.sin(2 * np.pi * t) + 0.5 * np.sin(5 * np.pi * t), x_range=[-2, 2], color=BLUE)

        fourier_formula = MathTex(r"\hat{f}(\xi) = \int f(t) e^{-2\pi i t \xi} dt", color=WHITE)
        prism = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_in_area(signal_waveform, 'A3', 'B6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(signal_waveform))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_in_area(dot_animation_group, 'C3', 'C6', scale_factor=0.7)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Gaussian Core: The Optimal Compromise", [
            "The Gaussian is the optimal compromise.",
            "It minimizes uncertainty in both domains.",
            "Narrowing in time broadens frequency.",
            "Widening in time narrows frequency.",
            "It balances both domains perfectly."
        ])

        colors = ["#FFC300", "#FF5733", "#C70039", "#900C3F", "#581845"]

        # Gaussian helper
        # Defined as mobject that doesn't use always_redraw for expensive things
        # But per instruction 11: Build once, update position/value/geometry in place.
        # Since FunctionGraph needs to be rebuilt, we use an updater.
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5], x_length=4, y_length=2, axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        sigma_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        gaussian = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(
            lambda t: np.exp(-t**2 / (2 * sigma_tracker.get_value()**2)), 
            color=colors[0]
        ))
        
        # Load Assets
        oscilloscope = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/oscilloscope.svg")
        metronome = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/metronome.svg")
        
        # Layout according to critic feedback
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'C3', 'E6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(oscilloscope, 'B2', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(metronome, 'F2', scale_factor=0.3)
        
        self.add(axes, gaussian, oscilloscope, metronome)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        self.play(sigma_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(colors[3])
        self.play(sigma_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(colors[4])
        self.play(sigma_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Uncertainty product is strictly bounded.", "Delta t times delta f is constant.", "Limit set by physical nature."]
        self.setup_layout("Formalizing Uncertainty", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        clock = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/clock.svg")
        tuningfork = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tuningfork.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula = MathTex(r"\Delta t \cdot \Delta f \geq \frac{1}{4\pi}", font_size=40, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        dt = MathTex(r"\Delta t", color=BLUE)
        df = MathTex(r"\Delta f", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(dt, 'C3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(df, 'C4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(clock, 'D3', scale_factor=0.4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dt), FadeIn(df), FadeIn(clock))
        self.play(dt.animate.scale(1.5), df.animate.scale(0.5))
        self.play(dt.animate.scale(0.66), df.animate.scale(2.0))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight constant
        constant = formula[0][6:] # Corrected slice for MathTex indexing of 1/(4pi)
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(constant, color="#33D4FF")
        self.place_at_grid(tuningfork, 'D5', scale_factor=0.4)
        
        self.play(Create(highlight), FadeIn(tuningfork))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bats use chirps for echolocation.",
            "Short duration provides distance resolution.",
            "Frequency sweep captures target signature."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Bat's Echolocation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        bat = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bat.svg")
        insect = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/insect.svg")
        
        self.place_at_grid(bat, 'B2', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(insect, 'D5', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(bat, insect)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        wave = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5 * np.sin(10 * t) * np.exp(-2 * (t - 0.5)**2), 0]),
            t_range=[0, 1],
            color="#FF5733"
        )
        self.place_at_grid(wave, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(wave))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        reflection = wave.copy().set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(wave.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(reflection))
        self.play(reflection.animate.shift(LEFT * 2.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        line = Line(start=bat.get_center(), end=insect.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        delta_t = Text("Δt", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(delta_t, 'D4', 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(line), Write(delta_t))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Uncertainty Principle: The Fourier Trade-off

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Musical Pulse
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental tension: You cannot have a note that is both infinitely short in time (a sharp click) and perfectly precise in pitch (a pure frequency).
sections.example: Visualizing a drum beat (short time, wide range of frequencies) vs. a long flute note (long time, precise frequency).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Fourier Bridge
sections.content: Briefly explain the Fourier Transform as a prism: it maps a signal from the Time Domain (where it happens) to the Frequency Domain (what it's made of).
sections.example: An animation showing a complex waveform being decomposed into its constituent sine waves, like a light beam hitting a prism.

sections.title: The Gaussian Core: The Optimal Compromise
sections.content: Explain that the Gaussian function is the unique mathematical bridge. It is the 'most compact' function in both domains. As the Gaussian narrows in time, its Fourier Transform broadens in frequency.
sections.example: A 'breathing' animation of a Gaussian curve narrowing; as it gets skinny, its Fourier counterpart grows wide and flat, illustrating the trade-off.

sections.title: Formalizing Uncertainty
sections.content: Present the mathematical inequality: Δt · Δf ≥ 1/(4π). Explain that the product of the widths (spreads) of the two domains is constrained by a constant.
sections.example: A 'seesaw' balance scale graphic where 'Time Resolution' sits on one side and 'Frequency Resolution' on the other; the fulcrum represents the constant limit.

sections.title: Application: The Bat's Echolocation
sections.content: Apply the principle to a real-world scenario. A bat needs to locate prey (needs short pulses) but also identify the prey (needs frequency information). The Uncertainty Principle dictates the bat's pulse design.
sections.example: A bat emitting a 'chirp'. Show the spectrogram: a short, wide-band signal allows for accurate distance timing, while the 'sweep' captures target-specific acoustic signatures.
